gap.description: Every ranking result is written by a gear e-commerce brand or a local Western gym marketing its own classes — none are written by someone who has actually trained in Thailand or works with Thai coaches. None cover the cultural/ceremonial layer (wai kru, ram muay, mongkhon, the role of music/rhythm in a fight), none explain why the 'art of 8 limbs' developed the way it did beyond a one-line history blurb, and none help a reader decide practically ('should I book a trip and train Muay Thai in Thailand, or is a kickboxing gym near me enough?'). No result speaks with authentic, lived Thai-camp authority.

weakness: History sections are superficial one-paragraph blurbs recycled across all 5 results, no primary sourcing
"Philosophy" and "which is better" sections stay abstract and generic, never grounded in a real camp or real fighters
E-E-A-T is weak site-wide: 3 of 5 results have no named author at all, and the 2 with bylines are generalist freelancers/marketing teams, not Thai practitioners
No result addresses total beginners' practical concerns (what a first class feels like, injury risk, what to bring) beyond generic gear upsells
recommended_angle: Write the comparison from inside an actual Chiang Mai camp with Thai coaches — keep the same practical technique/rules breakdown readers expect (so it still satisfies the query and can win the featured snippet with a clean comparison table), but layer in what none of the affiliate/gear sites can: the cultural roots (wai kru, ram muay, respect for kru), a lived explanation of why Muay Thai trains the way it does, and a warm, family-camp framing of 'if this sounds like you, here's what training it for real, in Thailand, actually feels like' — no warrior/hardcore posture, just genuine welcoming expertise.
